item: The erase never touches a marked data drive that is not there, cannot be identified, or changed during it (R809, R812), says so as a failure, and never closes its database connections then
summary: crypto_erase._drive_state: absent (no folder, an empty mount point, another drive's marker) or unidentified (a marker that cannot be read, a check that fails); then nothing under the data folder is read, erased, scoped or removed, the drive id is kept, stores the overrides keep elsewhere are erased and counted apart, and the result is a failure with no reassurance (S1 / S5). A drive that is there has its identity (resolved folder's device and inode, a held directory descriptor on POSIX, the marker id) re-checked before the first write and before every later drive step and close point; a change stops all work on it (S5 before the first write, S3 after). Lost during the erase: S3, plus S6 when the erase had already forgotten its id (never restored). Coordinator decision 1: SQLite deletes <db>-wal/-shm BY PATH when the last connection closes, so on a drive absent, unidentified, changed or lost the connections on it are pinned (src/database/drive_pin.py: out of every close, never freed) and S7 says its key stays in memory until the app is closed. DuckDB serves on such a drive (a file ATTACHed there, or an offload folder there) are taken out under their own lock and kept, every later serve close goes through drive_pin.close_or_keep, and an offload folder there is never removed. Re-checks compare the folder's file-system id too. The free-space overwrite writes nothing there. The CLI stops before opening anything (src/api/_panic_precheck.py), erases nothing and says so, exit 2 (1 when lost). Remaining window: path-based walks between a re-check and the writes after it (row 387). Strings x12 passed by Plan.
